Subject: Post-call: Archero inference mode fit & preliminary cost outline

Hi Elena — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery and three asks so we can build a tight cost/architecture recommendation for you: 

Recap (from call)
- Primary workload: EHR summarization + clinical QA assistant (avg response length ~200 tokens).
- Latency SLO: p95 <= 600ms for interactive flows; batch summarization OK at higher latency.
- Expected steady-state: ~1.2M generated tokens / day, peak QPS ~45 (short bursts to ~120).
- Data needs: PHI-sensitive; likely need VPC or dedicated controls.
- Preference: product team initially prefers Dedicated capacity for predictable latency, but procurement wants per-token pricing comparison for total cost clarity.

Three asks for our model: 
1) Can you confirm monthly active users and an estimate of monthly API calls (or attach a short sample of daily usage)?
2) Any required data residency/retention windows (e.g., 30/90/365 days)?
3) Who should we loop for procurement/legal (name + email)?

I attached a small CSV template (archero_usage_sample.csv) — if you can drop a row-level sample we’ll run a Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC/on-prem) TCO analysis with clear assumptions.

Next steps proposed:
- You supply the small usage sample and retention requirement (this week)
- We'll deliver a 2-page cost comparison + one-slide recommendation (within 3 business days after sample)
- Technical deep dive to validate integration points (30–45m) — propose Wed 9/9 or Thu 9/10 at 10:00 PT.

If the above sounds right, can you confirm who to include for procurement?

Thanks,
Elliot

Thanks Elliot — appreciate the clear recap. Quick answers below and I attached a small extract from our analytics pipeline.

- Monthly active users: ~18k clinicians (writes + reads).
- Monthly API calls (approx): 35M total calls; generated tokens ~36M tokens/month (we average ~200 generated tokens per call as you noted).
- Peak & steady-state: steady ~40 QPS, peak bursts up to ~140 QPS for short windows (10–15s).
- Data residency/retention: US-only; we store logs for 90 days, PHI must not exit our VPC unless under strict encryption & key controls.
- Procurement contact: Maria Gomez <maria.gomez@archero.com> (cc’d).

We would prefer a Dedicated capacity conversation given latency and PHI constraints, but we need the cost delta vs Hosted per-token and a Private VPC option if the Dedicated SLA/controls can’t meet our audit needs.

Forwarding Elena’s numbers. Naomi — tagging you for product/controls input. Rishi — can you run two sketches and flag assumptions we should call out to procurement?

Ask for Rishi (short):
- Sketch A (Hosted per-token): assumptions: 36M gen tokens/mo, 200 tokens/response, target p95 latency <=600ms. Include per-token cost, expected avg latency, and any scaling caveats (burst throttling).
- Sketch B (Dedicated reserved commit): assumptions: need to support 140 QPS peak with p95 <=600ms. Provide monthly reserved commit pricing options (1 GPU pool vs 2 smaller pools), cost of autoscale burst, and amortized infra + license.
- Sketch C (Private VPC/on-prem): rough delta to Dedicated once you add KMS/HSM and network egress constraints; include one-off onboarding and annual support.
- Please include a simple breakeven analysis: under what monthly token/QPS profile does Dedicated become cheaper than Hosted?

I started a prelim spreadsheet and attached (prelim_cost_model.xlsx). Keep this high-level — we’ll refine after the technical deep dive.

Thanks — can you aim EOD tomorrow? Elena, we’ll share the slides before the deep dive.

Subject: Re: Archero usage sample + ask to build quick TCO sketches

Hi Elena (and Maria),

Thanks for the usage dump — very helpful. Short summary of our two recommended paths and next steps: 

Path 1 — Hosted API (per-token)
- Monthly base: 36M generated tokens, estimate cost ~ $0.0009 per gen-token (preliminary public-model blended rate) -> ~ $32k/mo before volume discounts.
- Pros: fastest to go live, no onboarding, Redwood handles all infra.
- Cons: additional controls required for PHI (we can offer VPC peering and managed encryption but some customers prefer Dedicated for full isolation).

Path 2 — Dedicated Reserved Capacity (recommended if predictability & latency are priority)
- To support 140 QPS peaks at p95<=600ms we estimate a reserved pool equivalent to 5x A100-class instances with autoscale headroom. Preliminary monthly committed cost estimate: $58k–$78k/mo depending on GPU sizing and commit term.
- Autoscale bursts (pay-as-you-go) estimated additional $4k–$9k for typical peak patterns.
- Pros: predictable latency and isolated tenancy; easier to satisfy audit controls.
- Cons: higher committed cost vs low-volume Hosted. Breakeven with Hosted per-token at ~55–70M gen tokens/mo depending on discounts.

Path 3 — Private VPC / On-prem (audit-first customers)
- One-time onboarding + KMS integration: ~$45k–$70k (setup + compliance evidence packages). Annual platform fee + support add ~ $12k–$28k depending on retention SLA. Ongoing infra costs depend on customer cloud or on-prem hardware.
- Pros: maximal control for PHI and auditability.
- Cons: higher TCO and longer time-to-production.

Next steps:
- We’ll prepare a 2-slide summary with the above numbers and a one-sheet breakeven chart (Hosted vs Dedicated) by EOD today and send before the technical deep dive.
- Proposed deep dive: Thu 9/9 10:00 PT (30–45m) — please confirm.
- Maria: can you confirm procurement timelines and whether a standalone SOC2 attestation + KMS/HSM is a hard requirement for RFP?

I attached a short SOW outline we’d use to scope Dedicated onboarding (SOW_outline_draft.pdf). Happy to revise.

Cheers,
Rishi Malhotra
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
